title: Framing of charges - an underrated turning point in a trial
p1:
Many people think a trial truly begins when witnesses enter the courtroom.

But one of the most decisive moments often happens much earlier — when charges are framed.
p2:
A common misconception is that framing of charges is just a routine court step. It is not.

This is the stage where the court decides: "What exactly will the accused have to face during the trial?"

A poorly framed charge can change the entire direction of a case. A clearly defined charge creates a focused path for evidence, arguments, and defence strategy.
p3:
Framing of charges does not decide guilt or innocence. It simply identifies the allegations that deserve a full trial.

The surprising part? A strong defence often begins before the first witness speaks — by carefully examining whether the charges themselves are legally sustainable.

A small procedural decision can shape years of litigation.
conclusion: Have you ever considered how a decision made before the trial begins can influence the entire course of justice?
